**Extract:**

**HealthyMunch **

HealthyMunch is a social enterprise based in Country Z that provides nutritious, affordable meals to elderly and vulnerable people. Founded 5 years ago, HealthyMunch now serves over 500 customers daily through its meal delivery service and two community cafes.

As a social enterprise, HealthyMunch reinvests all profits into expanding its services and improving meal quality. Last year, it had revenue of \$750,000 and made a profit of \$50,000. The company employs 30 full-time staff and works with 50 volunteers.

HealthyMunch markets its services through a mix of traditional and digital methods. They distribute brochures in local community centers and doctor's offices, and have partnerships with local health services for referrals. Their social media presence focuses on sharing nutritional tips and customer testimonials. They also rely heavily on word-of-mouth recommendations from satisfied customers and their families.

To better understand its market, HealthyMunch conducts regular market research. They use a combination of surveys, focus groups, and analysis of customer order data. Recent findings show that there's growing demand for specialized diets (e.g., low-sodium, diabetic-friendly meals) and interest in cooking classes for family caregivers. They've also identified a potential new market segment of busy working adults looking for healthy, ready-made meals.

HealthyMunch is considering expanding its services to include nutrition education programs in local schools. This would require hiring specialised staff and developing new educational materials. The company estimates this expansion would cost \$100,000 initially but could increase revenue by 20% within two years.

However, HealthyMunch faces some challenges. Food costs have risen by 15% in the past year due to inflation, putting pressure on its margins. The company is also experiencing increased competition from for-profit meal delivery services targeting the elderly.

The board of directors is divided on whether to pursue the school program expansion or focus on improving efficiency in its current operations. They need to make a decision soon, as government grants for school nutrition programs will be available in 3 months.

HealthyMunch prides itself on its strong relationships with customers and the local community. It regularly conducts surveys to gather feedback and has a customer satisfaction rating of 92%.

**Appendix 1: HealthyMunch Financial Data**

| **Year** | **Revenue (\$000)** | **Profit (\$000)** | **Number of meals served daily** |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 750 | 50 | 500 |
| 2021 | 650 | 45 | 450 |
| 2020 | 550 | 35 | 400 |

Consider how the following two ways could help HealthyMunch respond to accusations it has made false claims about its products in promotional materials.

- Implementing transparent communication strategies
- Strengthening product quality assurance processes

Which approach is likely to be most effective in restoring customer trust? **Justify** your answer.

Refer to the following [insert ](https://cdn.savemyexams.com/uploads/2024/10/healthymunch-case-study.pdf)when answering the question
parts.solution_md:
Implementing transparent communication strategies involves openly addressing the accusations through clear, honest messaging **[Ap]**. HealthyMunch could publish detailed nutritional information and ingredient sourcing on their website and packaging **[Ap]**. This approach builds credibility by showing the company has nothing to hide and demonstrates accountability **[An]**. However, transparency alone may not be sufficient if the underlying product issues are not addressed **[An]**

Strengthening product quality assurance processes means implementing rigorous testing and verification systems for all health claims **[Ap]**. HealthyMunch could introduce third-party nutritional testing and obtain certifications from recognised health organisations **[Ap]**. This approach addresses the root cause of the problem by ensuring all promotional claims are accurate and evidence-based **[An]**. The investment in quality systems may increase costs but protects against future accusations **[An]**

Strengthening product quality assurance processes is likely to be most effective in restoring customer trust **[E]**. While transparent communication is important for immediate damage control, quality assurance prevents future problems and provides concrete evidence to support promotional claims **[E]**. Customers will have greater confidence in a company that can demonstrate rigorous testing and verification of their health claims through independent certification **[E]**. This approach also supports long-term reputation management and competitive advantage in the health-focused market **[E]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each approach identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the response strategy
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
>   - Add a final Evaluation (E):
>   
>     - Decide which approach is most effective
>     - Justify your choice
>     - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Implementing transparent communication strategies**
> 
>   - Open acknowledgement of accusations → builds credibility through honesty and accountability
>   - Publication of detailed nutritional data and sourcing information → allows customers to verify claims independently
>   - Regular updates on corrective actions taken → demonstrates ongoing commitment to accuracy
> - **Strengthening product quality assurance processes**
> 
>   - Third-party nutritional testing and verification → provides independent validation of health claims
>   - Certification from recognised health organisations → adds credibility and regulatory compliance
>   - Implementation of rigorous internal testing protocols → prevents future false claims and protects reputation
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Quality assurance processes will be most effective as they address root causes rather than just symptoms
>   - Transparent communication is necessary but insufficient without underlying product integrity
>   - Quality systems provide long-term protection and competitive advantage in health-focused markets

**Extract:**

Sports Safety Equipment (SSE)

SSE manufactures sports safety equipment in country Z. It is a public limited company which has been successful for over 30 years. The main product SSE manufactures is safety helmets for different sports, such as bicycle riding, cricket and skateboarding. SSE has one large factory making the safety helmets. The factory uses flow production. The production workers each specialise in one task on the production line. SSE’s raw materials are imported.

SSE sells its helmets in several other countries and is planning to expand into many more. It will need to carry out market research before entering new markets in other countries. Each country has different sports that are popular and the style of helmets varies from country to country.

SSE plans to build its own factories in its most important markets in other countries and will need to choose a suitable source of finance. The Human Resources Director has decided to use internal recruitment for the managers of the new factories. There will need to be effective communication between the managers of the new factories and SSE’s head office in country Z.

Most of SSE’s sales in country Z are through sports equipment shops. Customers like to try on the helmets to check they fit correctly. SSE currently sells its helmets in other countries through its website.

SSE is also increasing its product range. The latest new product being developed is a children’s cricket helmet. A break-even chart for this new product is shown in Appendix 3.

**Appendix 1**

**Extract from SSE’s website**

**If you want the best protection when playing sport then buy an SSE safety helmet!**

We supply a wide range of safety helmets for you when playing sport.

Whatever the sport - SSE produces a helmet for you.

You can order directly from this website by entering your head measurements below.

Get the perfect fit for you!

**Appendix 2**

**Email from SSE’s Managing Director to SSE’s Finance Director**

To: Finance Director

From: Managing Director

Date: 1 September 2023

Re: Demand for SSE’s products

Demand for SSE’s products in country Z is forecast to increase. Our government has imposed import tariffs on safety helmets. We may be able to increase our prices.

The exchange rate in country Z is expected to fall. However, other countries have introduced import quotas on safety helmets.

We will have to consider all the likely effects of these changes.

**Appendix 3**

**Projected weekly break-even chart for SSE’s new children’s cricket helmet**

![A graph showing the relationship between output in units (x-axis) and costs and revenue in dollars (y-axis) with lines for total revenue, total costs, and fixed costs.](assets/001-a-graph-showing-the-relationship-between-output-.png)

The maximum output and sales for this product is 1000 units per week

Consider the advantages and disadvantages of the following two ways to ensure products comply with legal controls on marketing when SSE expands into new international markets.

- Compliance checks
- Staff training programmes

Which way should SSE prioritise to ensure compliance with legal controls on marketing? **Justify** your answer.
parts.solution_md:
Compliance checks would allow SSE to systematically review their marketing materials and practices against specific legal requirements in each country **[Ap]**. For example, they could verify that helmet advertisements comply with safety claim regulations or consumer protection laws **[Ap]**. This would help identify potential legal violations before they occur, reducing the risk of fines or legal action **[An]**. However, these checks can be expensive to conduct regularly, especially across multiple countries with different legal frameworks **[Ap]**. This could increase operational costs and require specialist legal expertise **[An]**.

Staff training programmes would be more cost-effective for SSE in the long term. They could educate marketing teams about advertising standards and consumer protection laws in different countries **[Ap]**. This would help prevent legal violations from occurring in the first place **[Ap]** and create a culture of compliance throughout the organisation **[Ap]**. Training materials like online courses could provide accessible information about legal requirements, but staff may forget key details over time or new laws may be introduced. Regular updates and refresher training may therefore be needed to maintain effectiveness **[An]**.

Overall, SSE should prioritise staff training programmes, supported by periodic legal compliance audits **[E]**. While compliance checks are important for verification, training programmes will embed compliance knowledge directly into daily marketing decisions **[E]**. This is crucial as SSE expands internationally and marketing laws vary significantly between countries **[Ap]**. The proactive approach of training will help SSE avoid costly legal violations and maintain their reputation in new markets **[E]**.

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **Structure**
> 
> - Write one PEA paragraph for each point identified in the question:
> 
>   - Point: Identify the compliance method
>   - Evidence (Ap): Apply case study detail
>   - Analysis (An): Explain business impact
>   - Add a final Evaluation (E):
> 
> - Decide which method is most effective/practical
> 
>   - Justify your choice
>   - Compare and reject alternatives
> 
> **Marking approach**
> 
> - This is a levelled response answer in which the examiner determines how well you have demonstrated skills of application, analysis and evaluation
> 
>   - Application (4) – Use case study facts
>   - Analysis (4) – Chain effects clearly, using business terms
>   - Evaluation (4) – Balanced judgement, rejects others with reasoning
> 
> **Mark scheme**
> 
> - **Compliance checks**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Systematic review of marketing materials → identifies specific legal violations → prevents fines and legal action
>     - Expert assessment of advertising claims about helmet safety → ensures compliance with consumer protection laws → maintains credibility
>     - Regular monitoring of changing legal requirements → helps adapt marketing strategies → reduces compliance risks
>     - Independent verification provides assurance → builds confidence with regulators → protects company reputation
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Specialist legal expertise required → higher consultancy costs → increased operational expenses
>     - Time-consuming process across multiple countries → delays marketing campaigns → slower market entry
>     - Reactive approach only identifies problems after creation → may require costly material redesign
> 
> - **Staff training programmes**
> 
>   - **Advantages**
>   
>     - Educates marketing teams about local advertising laws → prevents violations at source → reduces legal risks
>     - Cost-effective once developed → can be rolled out across multiple markets → lower per-employee costs
>     - Creates compliance culture throughout organisation → embeds legal awareness → improves decision-making
>     - Online delivery enables quick updates → keeps staff informed of law changes → maintains current knowledge
>   - **Disadvantages**
>   
>     - Staff may forget training content over time → compliance knowledge deteriorates → increases violation risks
>     - Generic training may not cover specific country requirements → gaps in legal knowledge → potential non-compliance
>     - Requires regular updates as laws change → ongoing training costs → administrative burden
> 
> - **Conclusion**
> 
>   - Compliance checks: best for thorough verification and expert assessment of complex legal requirements
>   - Staff training programmes: best for embedding compliance knowledge and preventing violations proactively
>   - Practical approach: implement comprehensive staff training as foundation, supplemented by targeted audits for high-risk marketing materials or new market entries
